Thesis.proseOnly: States the numerator-shrinking claim and the selection inequality; the first worked figure follows in The data wall.

The data wall.teaches: Compare unique token supply against the compute-optimal need and the tokens actually processed.
The data wall.source: The data wall. WebText 10B unique, Chinchilla ~20 tok/param need of 30B, 167B processed at ~17 repeats — book values.

Measuring data value.teaches: Read how marginal ICR halves with each corpus doubling under the chapter's illustrative model.
Measuring data value.source: Diminishing returns and the ICR frontier. Normalized doublings are illustrative; the 1/(O·D) form is the chapter's.

The selection inequality.teaches: Judge whether a scorer's added time still leaves selection + subset training under the full-run bar.
The selection inequality.source: The selection inequality. The worked 128,117-image coreset on one H100 at 25% of peak is the book's example.

Static pruning.teaches: Identify which high-scored common example a rare-class floor displaces inside a fixed budget.
Static pruning.source: Coreset selection and Validating a reduced dataset. Scores, slices and the three-slot budget are illustrative.

Dynamic selection.teaches: Trace the score-query-annotate-expand-retrain loop and name who pays each stage's cost.
Dynamic selection.source: Active learning, human in the loop; the $5/label and $500k budget are the book's worked ROI.

Synthetic data and the unlabeled levers.teaches: Count the downstream tasks at which prepaid pretraining undercuts training from scratch.
Synthetic data and the unlabeled levers.source: Foundation-model amortization — 10,000 + 50N versus 1,000N GPU-hours, break-even at N >= 11 (book values).

Selection engineering: the data path tax.teaches: Match storage tier to the realized-bandwidth loss of scattered 4 KB reads, and pick the subset plan that materializes.
Selection engineering: the data path tax.source: The random-access penalty — ~375x HDD, ~14x SATA SSD, <2x NVMe (book's table).

Choosing a strategy.teaches: Find the run count where accumulated gross savings reaches the fixed curation cost.
Choosing a strategy.source: Amortization across training runs — the book's worked $30k setup and $6k per-run saving.
